h1: AI Product Videos for Home Brands, Shown in the Room They Fit
lead: Home shoppers need the product in a room, doing one job. One clear photo can become that scene without building a set.
card: Room scenes, cleaning demos, and organizing moments from one home product photo.

faq.q: Can I show a before-and-after of a closet?
faq.a: Yes, if the after state is something your product really does. Describe both states in plain words, and do not show a result the product cannot produce.

faq.q: Will furniture look the right size?
faq.a: Scale is the unreliable part. Mention a size in the description, such as a 24-inch round side table next to an armchair, and put the real dimensions on the listing.

faq.q: Does this work for sofas and beds?
faq.a: It can, when the photo shows the whole piece, including legs. Name a room large enough to hold it. Parts that are cut out of the photo will not be invented reliably.

faq.q: Can I start from a white-background photo?
faq.a: Yes. Keep the whole product in frame, including legs, handles, and cords. The scene can only use what the upload shows.

faq.q: Can I make a short cleaning demo?
faq.a: Yes. Use one visible mess, keep the angle steady, and show the product doing a single pass. A 10-second clip is 40 credits.

faq.q: What should I name in the scene?
faq.a: Name the room, nearby furniture, the light, and the one action shoppers need. Keep exact dimensions and materials in the listing.

faq.q: Can I run the clips as paid ads?
faq.a: Yes. Downloads are watermark-free and licensed for commercial use, including paid ads. Keep dimensions and capacity claims true to the item.

faq.q: Do I need a studio or a model?
faq.a: No for these clips. Rooms and adult hands are generated around your photo, at the credit cost shown before the job. A 6-second clip is 24 credits, 15 seconds is 60, and 30 seconds is 120. A failed job returns its credits.
